title: Angle-Angle Similarity Review Test
description: Review Angle-Angle similarity through missing angles, proof evidence, correspondence, and parallel-line reasoning.

questions.questionText: In a drawing for a ramp model, Triangle J has angles 42 degrees and 68 degrees. Triangle K has angles 68 degrees and 70 degrees. What is the best conclusion?
options: The triangles must be congruent by AA.
The triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles are similar only if all side lengths are equal.
The triangles are not similar because one angle is missing.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: The third angles are 70 degrees and 42 degrees, so two angle pairs match. That proves similarity by AA.

questions.questionText: During a shadow measurement lab, Triangle J has angles 35 degrees and 85 degrees. Triangle K has angles 35 degrees and 60 degrees. What is the best conclusion?
options: The triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles must be congruent by AA.
The triangles are similar because every pair of triangles has angle sum 180 degrees.
The information does not prove the triangles are similar by AA.
questions.correctAnswer: The information does not prove the triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: The angle sets do not create two matching angle pairs. Triangle angle sums alone do not prove similarity.

questions.questionText: While checking a scale drawing, One triangle has angles 38 degrees, 74 degrees, and 68 degrees. A second triangle has one angle 38 degrees. What other angle would prove similarity by AA?

74 degrees

66 degrees

questions.explanation: AA needs two matching angle pairs. The second triangle already matches 38 degrees, so a 74 degree angle would give a second matching pair.

questions.questionText: In a map inset problem, A student wants to prove two triangles are similar. The diagram shows a 40 degree angle in each triangle and a 75 degree angle in each triangle. Is that enough for AA similarity?
options: No, AA also requires proportional side lengths.
No, AA can prove congruence but not similarity.
Yes, two angle pairs are known to match.
Yes, because every triangle has the same side lengths.
questions.correctAnswer: Yes, two angle pairs are known to match.
questions.explanation: Two matching angle pairs prove the triangles are similar by AA; proportional sides then follow.

questions.questionText: In a drawing for a ramp model, Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF by AA. Angle A matches angle D, and angle B matches angle E. Which side correspondence follows?
options: Side AB corresponds to side EF.
Side AB corresponds to side DE.
Side AC corresponds to side DE.
Side BC corresponds to side DF.
questions.correctAnswer: Side AB corresponds to side DE.
questions.explanation: The order of the matching angles determines the order of corresponding vertices, so the matching sides must connect matching vertices.

questions.questionText: During a shadow measurement lab, Two triangles already have one pair of matching angles. Another pair is labeled 3x + 12 degrees and 60 degrees. What value of x would complete an AA similarity proof?
questions.explanation: Set the matching angles equal: 3x + 12 = 60, so x = 16.

questions.questionText: On a coordinate-grid sketch, Segment MN is parallel to a side of a larger triangle, creating a smaller triangle inside it. Which reason can prove the two triangles are similar?
options: Corresponding angles from parallel lines match, giving AA similarity.
The smaller triangle was translated, so the triangles are congruent.
Parallel lines make all side lengths equal.
The triangles are similar only after measuring every side.
questions.correctAnswer: Corresponding angles from parallel lines match, giving AA similarity.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines create matching corresponding angles. With the shared angle, there are two matching angle pairs, so AA proves similarity.

questions.questionText: In a folded-paper diagram, A scale factor between two triangles is 5/2. Which extra evidence would prove the triangles are similar by AA instead of only comparing side lengths?
options: One side in each triangle has the same length.
The triangles are drawn facing the same direction.
Two pairs of corresponding angles are congruent.
The perimeters have different values.
questions.correctAnswer: Two pairs of corresponding angles are congruent.
questions.explanation: AA similarity is based on matching angles. Two corresponding angle pairs are enough to prove the triangles are similar.

questions.questionText: While checking a scale drawing, Triangle R has angles 44 degrees, 71 degrees, and one unknown angle. Triangle S has angles 44 degrees and 65 degrees. What conclusion follows?
options: The triangles are congruent because two angles match.
The triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles are not similar because one angle is unknown.
The triangles are similar only if their longest sides match exactly.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: The unknown angle in Triangle R is 65 degrees. That gives two matching angle pairs, so AA proves similarity.

questions.questionText: In a bridge-truss diagram, A student says, "These triangles share one angle, so they must be similar." Which response best evaluates the proof?
options: The proof is complete because one angle pair proves AA.
The proof is complete only if both triangles are right triangles.
The proof is wrong because similar triangles cannot share angles.
The proof is incomplete because one matching angle pair is not enough.
questions.correctAnswer: The proof is incomplete because one matching angle pair is not enough.
questions.explanation: AA requires two matching angle pairs. A shared angle gives only one pair unless another angle match is established.
